Threading does not even begin to cover Internet scale data. It takes tens of thousands of computers with the memory maxed out to keep the index in RAM. These need to be replicated at at least one backup site a thousand miles away. There will be dozens of memory corruptions a day from cosmic rays, so everything has to constantly check itself and rebuild when necessary. When a computer dies, you have to load a hot spare from the hard drive data; the dead one simply gets turned off and left until the data center reaches full capacity. There cannot be very many choke points like master servers, because when a master falls it could knock a thousand slaves offline. Clusters of computers need to elect a leader when power turns on, and monitor the leader and elect a new one when the current one behaves badly. For efficiency and cost, it is a good idea to run the power supplies on high-voltage DC instead of AC. Data that is rarely accessed should be moved to slow-spinning hard drives to cut electric power.
